text: In 1637, legend says a single tulip bulb cost as much as a house in Amsterdam.
The star was the Semper Augustus, white petals with flames of red.
Its price climbed from about 1,200 guilders to a reported 10,000.
People traded bulbs still in the ground on paper contracts in taverns.
Then, in February 1637, at an auction in Harlem, nobody bid.
The story says the Dutch economy was ruined.
Historian Anne Goldgar searched the records and couldn't find anyone who went bankrupt.
Much of the drama comes from a book written 200 years later.
That's the Mirage. History's most famous bubble was partly a bubble of a story. So when you
hear everyone lost everything, check who's telling it. This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
